7. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion either direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
11. Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
12. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age including a child still in the womb.
13. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.

18. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and community environment that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Victim recovery is services provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.

21. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

Article 22
(1) Regional Governments may organize partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
7. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion either direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
11. Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
12. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age including a child still in the womb.
13. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
14. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government and/or community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
15. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children who are victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
16. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking, hereinafter referred to as Task Force is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of criminal acts of human trafficking in South Buton Regency.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and community environment that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Victim recovery is services provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of women and children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
21. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their children or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 27
(1) Regional Governments may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement the protection of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 9
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 7 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing protection to women and children from acts of violence;
c. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
d. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
(3) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII
INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 11
(1) The Regional Government establishes PPT in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), is established at the Regency and Sub-district levels.
(3) The membership of PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of the Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, researchers and academics.
(4) Further provisions regarding the Organization and Working Procedures of PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

6.8.rationale: The Indonesian regulation clearly involves victims/witnesses in the legal process and provides facilitation/assistance through judicial stages. Pasal 5 huruf h grants “kemudahan dalam proses peradilan” (facilitation in the judicial process) for victims and families. Pasal 17 huruf c provides “pendampingan ... sebagai saksi mulai dari proses penyidikan hingga putusan” (assistance as witnesses from investigation through verdict). These provisions were also present in retrieved passages, so the judge’s “Yes” is consistent with the source; the golden “No” appears incorrect.
